Academic CV

José Miguel Aragón-Jurado

Ph.D. in Computer Engineering | Assistant Professor

Graduate School of Information, Production and Systems (IPS) Waseda University, Japan Kitakyushu, Japan ORCID 0000-0002-9835-8793

Ph.D. in Computer Engineering and Assistant Professor at Waseda University (Japan), previously a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Cádiz (Spain). Accredited as Associate Professor by ANECA in 2025. My research focuses on sustainable computing, combining compiler optimization, artificial intelligence, and evolutionary computation to reduce the environmental impact of software systems, with applications in green software, intelligent transportation, and software security through code obfuscation. Author of 12 journal papers (9 Q1, 3 Q2) and 20+ international conference papers, including CORE A/A/B venues. Research stays in Japan, Canada, and Belgium have led to ongoing international collaborations in sustainable AI and evolutionary computation.

Research Interests

  • Green and Sustainable Computing: Energy-aware software design, optimization, and environmental impact reduction across computing platforms.
  • Compiler Optimization and Evolutionary Computation: Automatic software tailoring, metaheuristics, and cooperative co-evolution for performance-energy trade-offs.
  • Software Security and Code Obfuscation: Optimization-driven source code protection and obfuscation methods for constrained and low-power environments.
  • Intelligent Transportation Systems and Sustainable Mobility: AI and predictive models for greener public transport operations, eco-driving, and emission-aware mobility planning.

Assistant Professor

Waseda University

April 2026 - Present

Kitakyushu, Japan

Current faculty appointment at Waseda University.

Postdoctoral Researcher (FPU Fellow)

University of Cadiz

July 2025 - March 2026

Cadiz, Spain

  • Conducted postdoctoral research on modern compiler optimizations and their impact on runtime and energy consumption.
  • Designed several experimental frameworks to evaluate compiler configurations on web browsers, CUDA applications on embedded GPUs, and Unity-based video games.
  • Analyzed optimization managers in LLVM and their effect on performance and energy efficiency.
  • Published 3 papers in JCR-indexed journals (2 Q1 and 1 Q2) and 5 conference papers.
Predoctoral Researcher (FPU Fellow)

University of Cadiz

January 2023 - July 2025

Cadiz, Spain

  • Completed the Ph.D. thesis 'Software Optimization for the Green Internet of Things'.
  • Proposed and solved 3 novel compiler optimization problems (SCOP, gSCOP, FROP) using evolutionary algorithms and LLVM, achieving up to 62% faster runtimes and 58% energy savings.
  • Designed adaptive software optimization frameworks for energy-efficient IoT, gaming, and embedded systems.
  • Developed ML-based models (MEPBO, SUTRA, ML-EPBO) for hybrid bus systems, achieving daily reductions of nearly 300 kg of CO2 and 110 liters of fuel.
  • Introduced the TSOP obfuscation model and created the C3GA algorithm, improving code protection by up to 405x in low-power environments.
  • Published 9 journal papers (7 Q1, 2 Q2) and 16+ conference papers, including CORE A/A* venues.
  • Conducted international research stays in Canada and Japan, leading to ongoing collaborations and joint publications.
Research Assistant
